To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the best algorithms for outlier detection are based on the nearest neighbor approach; (2) the LOF and HBOS algorithms are good alternatives for outlier detection; (3) the LOF algorithm is more robust than other methods; and (4) the HBOS algorithm has the lowest memory consumption

(1) the performance of algorithms is strongly dataset dependent, (2) the performance of an algorithm is not a reliable indicator for the performance of its implementation, (3) the performance of implementations of the same algorithm is strongly dependent on the dataset and the implementation, and (4) the performance of a single algorithm is not a sufficient indicator for the performance on a given dataset.

(i) LOF is the best algorithm in terms of accuracy, (ii) it is also one of the fastest, but (iii) the most memory consuming, (iv) it has a high robustness and (v) it is the only method that can deal with missing values.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: (i) How well can the selected outlier detection algorithms perform on a variety of real-world datasets?
the following questions: (1) How do the algorithms compare on different data sets, in terms of precision, recall, F-score, running time, and memory consumption?
the evaluation of outlier detection methods in terms of their scalability, robustness and memory consumption.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the outlier detection methods is highly dependent on the characteristics of the underlying datasets.
the best method is not always the best.
there is no single best algorithm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no one-size-fits-all algorithm for outlier detection.
the best algorithm is the one that fits your problem best.
the algorithms are not only different from each other in the way they work but also have different strengths and weaknesses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there is no single best algorithm for all scenarios.
there is no single method that is best suited for all outlier detection problems.
there is no single algorithm that can be considered the best in all aspects.
